report.rationale: Borescopy directly shows widespread mineral deposits narrowing exchanger channels, and controlled testing finds heat-transfer coefficient 39% below the clean reference at matched flow. Elevated temperature approach supports fouling. Normal inlet pressure, absent cavitation vibration, confirmed closed bypass, agreeing temperature sensors, and a deficit persisting across stable loads strongly disfavor the alternatives.

Borescopy directly shows widespread mineral deposits narrowing exchanger channels, and controlled testing finds heat-transfer coefficient 39% below the clean reference at matched flow. Elevated temperature approach supports fouling. Normal inlet pressure, absent cavitation vibration, confirmed closed bypass, agreeing temperature sensors, and a deficit persisting across stable loads strongly disfavor the alternatives.

The controlled test shows a 39% reduction in heat-transfer coefficient at matched flow, supported by an approach temperature 8.4 C above the clean baseline. Independently confirmed near-commanded flow, adequate inlet pressure, and absent cavitation vibration argue against pump cavitation. Verified bypass closure and sensor agreement weaken valve and sensor explanations. Steady sub-design load makes a load-only explanation unlikely.

At matched flow, the heat-transfer coefficient is 39% below the clean reference, and temperature approach is 8.4 C above baseline. Overdue cleaning supports fouling. Stable inlet pressure, near-commanded flow, independently confirmed bypass closure, agreeing temperature sensors, and a deficit persisting across stable loads argue against the alternatives.

The controlled test shows a 39% reduction in heat-transfer coefficient at matched flow, supported by an elevated temperature approach. Command and independent position feedback both indicate a closed bypass. Near-commanded flow, adequate inlet pressure, absent cavitation vibration, agreeing temperature sensors, and a deficit persisting across stable loads strongly disfavor the alternatives.

Exchanger approach is 8.4 C above its clean baseline despite near-commanded flow, normal ambient conditions, and a cooling deficit persisting across three stable loads. Adequate inlet pressure, agreeing temperature sensors, and independently confirmed bypass closure weaken competing diagnoses. The uncorroborated pump hum leaves cavitation as a residual possibility, but direct exchanger verification is still needed.
Deterministic arithmetic mean of independent agent probabilities.

The controlled test shows a heat-transfer coefficient 39% below the clean reference at matched flow, strongly supporting fouling. Near-commanded flow, adequate inlet pressure, normal motor current, and absent cavitation vibration argue against a pump fault. Independent bypass closure, agreeing temperature sensors, and steady process load weaken the other alternatives.

The controlled test shows a 39% reduction in heat-transfer coefficient at matched flow, supported by an approach temperature 8.4 C above the clean baseline. Agreement between temperature sensors, near-commanded flow, adequate pump inlet pressure, a verified closed bypass, and steady below-design load strongly favor exchanger fouling over the alternatives.

The controlled test found heat-transfer coefficient 39% below the clean reference at matched flow, strongly supporting exchanger fouling. The bypass is commanded and independently confirmed closed; temperature sensors agree, pump inlet pressure exceeds the cavitation margin, and flow is near command. Persistence across three stable loads argues against a transient.

The exchanger approach is 8.4 C above its clean baseline despite normal inlet temperature and near-commanded main-loop flow. Independent checks confirm the bypass is closed and temperature sensors agree. Stable inlet pressure above the cavitation margin and steady process load further favor fouling, although exchanger degradation has not been directly confirmed.

Borescopy directly revealed widespread mineral deposition narrowing multiple exchanger channels. This resolves the principal verification gap in the supplied reports and corroborates their reported matched-flow heat-transfer degradation. Their agreement reflects overlapping evidence, not independent confirmations.
